checks: corpus is 11,979 findings across 23 detectors; every call is capped at 100 results (an unfiltered call and a filtered one both return 100), so per-detector counts from this endpoint are 'up to 100' and a full sweep needs ~120 calls

CRITICAL is reserved for the scheduler's 31 node failures plus the one hardware fault -- it tracks availability, not money

checks: 121 filesystem findings all resolve to pvc/scratch-lustre-02 at score 0.88, nodes at 0.31 -- one cause, not 121 problems

array-task findings resolve to their array at score 1.0 with each machine at ~0.14; three different task findings gave 3 distinct culprit(s): {'array/65192801012', 'array/31811330654', 'array/10966139174'}
the spread across machines IS the evidence the machines are innocent
a finding with no rootCauses returns findings: [] and a message -- that is correct behaviour, not a failure (1 of the 6 detectors tried)
but the volume answer quotes the ratio of whichever finding you ask about: per-node ratios run 28.3x-45.5x, so the same incident reads 'rose 28.3x' or 'rose 45.5x'
and its second chain hop (gpu_sm_utilization abrupt_drop -91.4%) is a constant in api/main.py; the real telemetry on those 121 nodes shows 31.4% vs 36.4% the week before -- a 5-point dip
causal.verdict: The best endpoint in the API. Everything ranked should pass through it first.
causal.change: Quote one volume-level latency figure, and derive the utilization hop from telemetry or drop it.

checks: resources: 77,399 ({'k8s:pod': 74849, 'k8s:job': 2129, 'k8s:node': 225, 'k8s:namespace': 195, 'k8s:persistentvolumeclaim': 1})
one hop from the volume returns 500 nodes / 611 edges, but the volume has 2,537 MOUNTS edges: api/main.py:142 caps the node set at 500 with no flag in the response
the cap is applied before edges are gathered, so hop_count=2 returns 500 nodes and only 5 edges -- fewer than one hop, and a graph whose nodes are mostly unconnected
pods mounting the volume were active on 159 machines during the episode, but only 121 have a finding, so the graph is wider than the detector's blast radius
neighbor.verdict: Use it to check whether a 'cluster of problems' shares a dependency.
neighbor.change: Return edge direction and type counts in the response so a caller can walk it without the parquet.

checks: 24 rules armed, 1 reporting CLEAR
rules::gpu-pcie-saturated has never fired: peak PCIe on this estate is 4,240 MB/s of a 15,754 MB/s link (27%), so data movement is not the bottleneck -- a negative result worth as much as a finding
the rules' own text withholds cause on purpose (node-elevated-failure-rate reports a rate, not a reason), which is why case 6 had to triage all 113 itself
rules.verdict: Read it alongside the findings. A CLEAR rule is evidence.

checks: every state matches our groupby to the hour: COMPLETED 229,041, CANCELLED 203,930, TIMEOUT 107,952, FAILED 50,033, NODE_FAIL 2,028, UNDECODED_11 1,021

checks: it reports median SM utilization plus share_under_5pct and share_over_80pct per width band, and its own caveat says to read the shares, not the median -- correct, because the distribution is bimodal
